title: EMPLOYEE REQUEST
body: {name} would like to attend an art conference.

choices.label: APPROVE
choices.outcome: {name} comes back from the conference with a notebook full of ideas.

choices.label: DECLINE
choices.outcome: {name} accepts the answer, but it is noted.

title: TEAM FRICTION
body: {name} and another member of {their} team keep butting heads, and it is starting to show in the work.

choices.label: MEDIATE
choices.outcome: You sit them both down. It is an awkward hour, but they agree to keep it professional.

choices.label: STAY OUT OF IT
choices.outcome: You leave them to sort it out themselves. The mood on the team stays sour for weeks.

title: EQUIPMENT FAILURE
body: A development workstation has failed.

choices.label: REPLACE
choices.outcome: A replacement machine is on the desk by the end of the day.

choices.label: MAKE DO
choices.outcome: The team shares machines while a fix is arranged.

title: EMPLOYEE REQUEST
body: {name} has found a systems programming workshop and would like the studio to cover it.

choices.label: APPROVE
choices.outcome: {name} returns sharper, and clearly grateful.

choices.label: NOT THIS QUARTER
choices.outcome: {name} says {they} understands, though the disappointment shows.

title: EMPLOYEE REQUEST
body: {name} has found a game design summit and would like the studio to cover it.

choices.label: APPROVE
choices.outcome: {name} returns sharper, and clearly grateful.

choices.label: NOT THIS QUARTER
choices.outcome: {name} says {they} understands, though the disappointment shows.

title: EMPLOYEE REQUEST
body: {name} has found a narrative craft retreat and would like the studio to cover it.

choices.label: APPROVE
choices.outcome: {name} returns sharper, and clearly grateful.

choices.label: NOT THIS QUARTER
choices.outcome: {name} says {they} understands, though the disappointment shows.

title: EMPLOYEE REQUEST
body: {name} has found a game audio conference and would like the studio to cover it.

choices.label: APPROVE
choices.outcome: {name} returns sharper, and clearly grateful.

choices.label: NOT THIS QUARTER
choices.outcome: {name} says {they} understands, though the disappointment shows.

title: EMPLOYEE REQUEST
body: {name} has found a software testing certification course and would like the studio to cover it.

choices.label: APPROVE
choices.outcome: {name} returns sharper, and clearly grateful.

choices.label: NOT THIS QUARTER
choices.outcome: {name} says {they} understands, though the disappointment shows.

title: EMPLOYEE REQUEST
body: {name} has found a production management course and would like the studio to cover it.

choices.label: APPROVE
choices.outcome: {name} returns sharper, and clearly grateful.

choices.label: NOT THIS QUARTER
choices.outcome: {name} says {they} understands, though the disappointment shows.

title: SPEAKING INVITATION
body: A conference has invited {name} to give a talk about {their} work here.

choices.label: SEND THEM
choices.outcome: {name} represents the studio well. A few CVs arrive the week after.

choices.label: TOO BUSY
choices.outcome: The slot passes to someone from another studio.

title: EMPLOYEE REQUEST
body: {name} wants to open-source a small internal tool {they} built.

choices.label: ALLOW IT
choices.outcome: The tool picks up a following, and the studio's name travels with it.

choices.label: KEEP IT IN-HOUSE
choices.outcome: {name} shrugs and moves on.

title: MENTORING
body: {name} has been quietly coaching a newer teammate for weeks.

choices.label: RECOGNISE IT
choices.outcome: You thank {name} in front of the team. Both of them stand a little taller.

choices.label: LET IT RIDE
choices.outcome: The mentoring continues, unremarked.

title: EMPLOYEE REQUEST
body: {name} is asking for a second monitor.

choices.label: BUY IT
choices.outcome: A small thing that makes {their} day noticeably smoother.

choices.label: NOT RIGHT NOW
choices.outcome: {name} makes do with one screen.

title: SOFTWARE LICENSE
body: The studio's toolchain licenses are up for renewal, and the price has gone up.

choices.label: RENEW
choices.outcome: Paid, grumbled about, forgotten by Friday.

choices.label: DOWNGRADE THE TIER
choices.outcome: The cheaper tier is missing a few things the team relied on.

title: FACILITIES
body: Someone has started a thread about standing desks.

choices.label: KIT OUT THE FLOOR
choices.outcome: A round of new desks arrives. The floor likes it.

choices.label: NOTE THE FEEDBACK
choices.outcome: The thread goes quiet on its own.

title: THE COFFEE MACHINE
body: The coffee machine has died. Morale is measurably worse by 10am.

choices.label: REPLACE IT PROPERLY
choices.outcome: The new machine is better than the old one. A small win.

choices.label: INSTANT FOR NOW
choices.outcome: A jar of instant appears next to the kettle. It is not the same.

title: A QUIET WORD
body: {name} looks worn down. {they} has not said anything, but it is obvious.

choices.label: SEND THEM HOME FOR A WEEK
choices.outcome: {name} comes back steadier. The work waited.

choices.label: KEEP AN EYE ON IT
choices.outcome: You make a note to check in later.

title: FAMILY EMERGENCY
body: {name} needs to take time off at short notice for a family matter.

choices.label: OF COURSE
choices.outcome: {name} is grateful, and remembers it.

choices.label: AFTER THIS MILESTONE
choices.outcome: {name} stays, distracted and quietly resentful.

title: SABBATICAL REQUEST
body: {name} has been here a long time and is asking for an unpaid month off.

choices.label: GRANT IT
choices.outcome: {name} returns recharged and full of ideas.

choices.label: DECLINE
choices.outcome: {name} accepts it, but something has shifted.

title: GOOD NEWS
body: {name} is getting married and would like two weeks off.

choices.label: CONGRATULATE THEM
choices.outcome: The whole floor signs a card. {name} beams for a month.

choices.label: GRANT THE MINIMUM
choices.outcome: {name} takes the statutory leave and nothing more is said.

title: OUTSIDE OFFER
body: {name} has been approached by another studio and is being honest with you about it.

choices.label: MATCH IT
choices.outcome: {name} stays. The raise is real money, but so is losing {them}.

choices.label: WISH THEM WELL
choices.outcome: You do not counter. {name} has not decided yet, but the odds are not good.

title: CREDITS
body: {name} feels {their} contribution to the last game was under-credited.

choices.label: FIX THE CREDITS
choices.outcome: An updated credits list goes out. {name} feels seen.

choices.label: EXPLAIN THE CALL
choices.outcome: {name} listens, unconvinced.

title: WORK ANNIVERSARY
body: It is {name}'s work anniversary with the studio.

choices.label: MARK IT
choices.outcome: Cake, a short speech, a small bonus. {name} is touched.

choices.label: LET IT PASS
choices.outcome: Nobody mentions it. {name} notices that nobody mentions it.

title: TECHNICAL DEBT
body: {name} wants two weeks to pay down the worst of the codebase's technical debt.

choices.label: APPROVE THE CLEANUP
choices.outcome: Progress slows, then rebounds cleaner than before.

choices.label: AFTER SHIP
choices.outcome: The debt stays on the pile. So does the frustration.

title: EMPLOYEE REQUEST
body: {name} has drafted a studio art style guide and wants time to finish it.

choices.label: GIVE THEM THE TIME
choices.outcome: The guide pays off on every project after it.

choices.label: SHELVE IT
choices.outcome: The draft sits in a folder nobody opens.

title: PLAYTEST
body: {name} thinks the current build needs a proper external playtest before it goes further.

choices.label: RUN IT
choices.outcome: The findings sting, but the game is better for them.

choices.label: TRUST THE TEAM
choices.outcome: Development continues on instinct.

title: A WORD FROM PRODUCTION
body: {name} is worried the current project is drifting past what the team can finish well.

choices.label: CUT SOMETHING
choices.outcome: A hard conversation, then a tighter plan everyone believes in.

choices.label: PUSH ON
choices.outcome: The team keeps going. The unease does not go away.

title: TEAM LUNCH
body: The team has been heads-down for weeks. Someone suggests a proper lunch out.

choices.label: YOUR TREAT
choices.outcome: Two hours away from the desks does more than two hours at them.

choices.label: MAYBE FRIDAY
choices.outcome: The idea fades. Everyone eats at their desk again.

title: INTERNAL GAME JAM
body: The team wants to run a two-day internal game jam.

choices.label: BLOCK OUT THE TIME
choices.outcome: Nothing shippable comes out of it, but the floor is buzzing for a week.

choices.label: NOT THIS SPRINT
choices.outcome: The jam is postponed indefinitely.

title: THE OFFICE DOG
body: Someone has started bringing their dog in. Opinions vary.

choices.label: ALLOW IT
choices.outcome: Morale up, allergies down a bit, net positive.

choices.label: SET A POLICY
choices.outcome: A polite no. The dog stays home. So does a little goodwill.

title: THE OFFICE PLAYLIST
body: A low-grade dispute about the shared speaker has been running for a fortnight.

choices.label: BUY EVERYONE HEADPHONES
choices.outcome: The speaker goes quiet. So does the argument.

choices.label: LET THEM SORT IT
choices.outcome: The rota holds for a week, then collapses again.

title: A HONEST RETRO
body: The last project's retrospective turned unusually frank.

choices.label: ACT ON IT
choices.outcome: You commit to two concrete changes. The team watches to see if you mean it.

choices.label: THANK THEM AND MOVE ON
choices.outcome: The notes are filed. The team notices they were filed.

title: THE LANDLORD
body: The building's owner is signalling a rent increase at renewal.

choices.label: NEGOTIATE HARD
choices.outcome: You hold most of the line. It costs a tense meeting and a favour.

choices.label: ABSORB IT
choices.outcome: The higher rent is now just a fact of the month.

title: POWER CUT
body: A neighbourhood power cut has taken the office offline for the afternoon.

choices.label: SEND EVERYONE HOME
choices.outcome: A lost afternoon, cleanly. People pick it up tomorrow.

choices.label: WAIT IT OUT
choices.outcome: Half the team loses unsaved work when it flickers back.

title: BACKUP SCARE
body: A near-miss with the version control server has everyone rattled about backups.

choices.label: PAY FOR PROPER BACKUPS
choices.outcome: Offsite, automated, tested. One less thing to lie awake about.

choices.label: TIGHTEN THE MANUAL PROCESS
choices.outcome: A new checklist. It works until someone forgets it.

title: PRESS INTEREST
body: A games outlet wants to run a feature on the studio.

choices.label: GIVE THEM ACCESS
choices.outcome: The piece is warm and widely read. Good for the name.

choices.label: POLITELY DECLINE
choices.outcome: The feature runs about a different studio.

title: THE COMMUNITY
body: Players have built an ambitious mod for one of your games and are asking for a nod.

choices.label: SIGNAL-BOOST IT
choices.outcome: You share it everywhere. The community glows; a few new fans arrive.

choices.label: STAY QUIET
choices.outcome: The mod does fine without you. The makers notice the silence.

title: CHARITY BUNDLE
body: A charity bundle organiser has asked to include one of your older games.

choices.label: DONATE A SLOT
choices.outcome: Costs a bit of revenue, buys a lot of goodwill.

choices.label: DECLINE
choices.outcome: A reasonable business call that still feels a little cold.

title: LOCAL DEV MEETUP
body: The local game-dev meetup is looking for a venue and a host.

choices.label: HOST IT AT THE STUDIO
choices.outcome: Pizza, demos, and three promising people you now know by name.

choices.label: PASS IT ON
choices.outcome: Another studio hosts. You hear it went well.

title: POACHING SEASON
body: A recruiter has been messaging half the team on the same day.

choices.label: RALLY THE FLOOR
choices.outcome: A frank all-hands about where the studio is going steadies most of them.

choices.label: HOPE IT BLOWS OVER
choices.outcome: A couple of people take the calls. Nothing happens yet.

title: THE ACCOUNTANT CALLS
body: The books need a proper going-over before a filing deadline.

choices.label: BRING IN A PRO
choices.outcome: Clean books, a fee, and no more late-night spreadsheet dread.

choices.label: DO IT YOURSELF
choices.outcome: It gets done. It eats a weekend that should not have been eaten.

title: CONFERENCE BOOTH
body: There is a chance to take a small booth at a regional games conference.

choices.label: TAKE THE BOOTH
choices.outcome: A banner, a demo station, and a mailing list that is suddenly worth having.

choices.label: SKIP IT THIS YEAR
choices.outcome: The budget stays put.

title: A ROUGH WEEK ONLINE
body: One of your games is getting piled on over a bug that shipped.

choices.label: SHIP A FIX FAST
choices.outcome: A quick patch and a straight apology turn the mood around.

choices.label: LET IT PASS
choices.outcome: The noise dies down on its own, but it leaves a mark.

title: FAN MAIL
body: A stack of genuinely heartfelt letters about one of your games has arrived.

choices.label: READ THEM TO THE FLOOR
choices.outcome: Ten minutes that reminds everyone why they do this.

choices.label: PIN A FEW UP
choices.outcome: They go on the wall by the kitchen. People stop and read them.

title: HEATWAVE
body: The office air conditioning cannot keep up with the week's heat.

choices.label: BUY PORTABLE UNITS
choices.outcome: Not elegant, but the floor is workable again by lunch.

choices.label: TOUGH IT OUT
choices.outcome: Concentration melts along with everything else.

title: INTERNSHIP
body: A nearby course has asked whether the studio would take a summer intern.

choices.label: TAKE ONE ON
choices.outcome: It costs some senior time now; one of them is worth hiring later.

choices.label: NOT THIS YEAR
choices.outcome: The slot goes elsewhere.

title: THE UNIT NEXT DOOR
body: Building work in the neighbouring unit has made the office genuinely loud.

choices.label: PAY FOR ACOUSTIC PANELS
choices.outcome: The worst of it is dampened within a day.

choices.label: HAND OUT EARPLUGS
choices.outcome: People cope. Deep work does not.

title: AN UNEXPECTED SPIKE
body: An old game of yours is suddenly trending again after a streamer picked it up.

choices.label: LEAN IN
choices.outcome: A quick sale and a social push turn the moment into real momentum.

choices.label: ENJOY IT QUIETLY
choices.outcome: The spike fades in a fortnight, unremarked.

title: SMALL COMFORTS
body: The team's keyboards and chairs are visibly past their best.

choices.label: REFRESH THE LOT
choices.outcome: A dull purchase that everyone quietly appreciates for months.

choices.label: REPLACE THE WORST ONES
choices.outcome: A few people get new kit. The rest keep waiting.

title: A FILM CREW
body: A small documentary about local studios wants a day of filming.

choices.label: LET THEM IN
choices.outcome: A distracting day; a genuinely nice piece of press three months later.

choices.label: DECLINE
choices.outcome: The crew films elsewhere.

title: LOCALISATION
body: A localisation house has offered a good rate to translate one of your games.

choices.label: COMMISSION IT
choices.outcome: New regions, a modest cost, a wider audience for the back catalogue.

choices.label: NOT YET
choices.outcome: The game stays in one language for now.

title: INDUSTRY MENTORSHIP
body: An industry body wants senior staff to mentor newcomers from underrepresented backgrounds.

choices.label: SIGN THE STUDIO UP
choices.outcome: A few hours a month, well spent. It says something true about the place.

choices.label: MAYBE NEXT INTAKE
choices.outcome: The form goes in a drawer.

title: CRUNCH VOLUNTEER
body: {name} is offering to pull a weekend to hit the milestone.

choices.label: THANK THEM, BUT NO
choices.outcome: You move the milestone instead. {name} is surprised, then relieved.

choices.label: ACCEPT THE OFFER
choices.outcome: The milestone lands. {name} is running on fumes by Monday.

title: EMPLOYEE REQUEST
body: {name} has an idea for an internal tool that could save the team hours a week.

choices.label: FUND A PROTOTYPE
choices.outcome: A week lost now, paid back within a month.

choices.label: ADD IT TO THE BACKLOG
choices.outcome: The idea joins a hundred others nobody will get to.

title: A DESIGN DISAGREEMENT
body: {name} strongly disagrees with the direction a core system is taking.

choices.label: HEAR IT OUT PROPERLY
choices.outcome: An hour on the whiteboard produces a better third option.

choices.label: KEEP THE CURRENT PLAN
choices.outcome: The plan holds. {name} implements it without enthusiasm.

title: REMOTE REQUEST
body: {name} needs to move away for personal reasons and is asking to work remotely.

choices.label: MAKE IT WORK
choices.outcome: Some logistics, a webcam, and you keep someone you would have lost.

choices.label: IT HAS TO BE IN PERSON
choices.outcome: {name} starts looking for something closer to home.

title: HEALTH
body: {name} has had a health scare and is being careful about hours.

choices.label: PROTECT THEIR SCHEDULE
choices.outcome: You quietly rebalance the load. {name} does not forget it.

choices.label: BUSINESS AS USUAL
choices.outcome: {name} keeps up appearances and pays for it.

title: AWARD NOMINATION
body: One of your games has been longlisted for a regional development award.

choices.label: GO TO THE CEREMONY
choices.outcome: You do not win, but the night is good for the team and the name.

choices.label: SKIP THE CEREMONY
choices.outcome: A line in a newsletter. The team hears about it secondhand.

title: PIPELINE PROBLEM
body: {name} keeps getting blocked waiting on work from another discipline.

choices.label: FIX THE HANDOFF
choices.outcome: A short process change unclogs the pipe for everyone.

choices.label: WORK AROUND IT
choices.outcome: {name} finds a workaround. The block is still there for the next person.

title: LONG WEEKEND
body: A public holiday falls on a Friday. Someone asks about making it a four-day weekend.

choices.label: GIVE THE FLOOR THE DAY
choices.outcome: A rested team on Tuesday is worth more than a worked Friday.

choices.label: NORMAL FRIDAY
choices.outcome: Half the floor takes leave anyway; the other half resents it.

title: AN UNEXPECTED PARCEL
body: A hardware maker has sent over a box of new development kits, no strings stated.

choices.label: READ THE FINE PRINT FIRST
choices.outcome: Nothing hidden. The team gets nice new toys and a small speed-up.

choices.label: SEND IT BACK
choices.outcome: Better safe. The kits go back unopened.

title: VOLUNTEER DAY
body: A local school is asking for volunteers to run a coding afternoon.

choices.label: SEND A COUPLE OF PEOPLE
choices.outcome: An afternoon of lost work and a genuinely good deed.

choices.label: DECLINE POLITELY
choices.outcome: The school finds someone else.

title: UPSTREAM BUG
body: {name} has traced a nasty bug to a third-party library, not your code.

choices.label: PATCH IT AND UPSTREAM THE FIX
choices.outcome: Extra work now; goodwill and a fixed dependency later.

choices.label: WORK AROUND IT LOCALLY
choices.outcome: A hack that works, and a comment apologising for itself.

title: SETTLING IN
body: {name} is still finding their feet weeks after joining.

choices.label: PAIR THEM WITH A BUDDY
choices.outcome: A week of shadowing and {name} clicks into place.

choices.label: SINK OR SWIM
choices.outcome: {name} gets there eventually, the hard way.

title: CONFERENCE TICKETS
body: The studio has two spare passes to a major industry conference.

choices.label: RUN A FAIR LOTTERY
choices.outcome: Two happy people, and a transparent process the rest respect.

choices.label: SEND THE LEADS
choices.outcome: The obvious choice, and a slightly sour one.

title: SIDE PROJECT
body: {name} is making a small game of their own in the evenings and has been upfront about it.

choices.label: ENCOURAGE IT
choices.outcome: {name} brings the energy back into the day job. Everyone wins.

choices.label: REMIND THEM OF THE CONTRACT
choices.outcome: {name} complies, and dims a little.

title: BREAK-IN
body: Someone broke into the office overnight and took two laptops.

choices.label: REPLACE AND UPGRADE SECURITY
choices.outcome: A bad morning, a real bill, and a lock that actually works now.

choices.label: CLAIM ON INSURANCE AND WAIT
choices.outcome: The excess still stings, and the team is jumpy for a fortnight.

title: STREAMER PARTNERSHIP
body: A mid-size streamer wants early access to your next game in exchange for coverage.

choices.label: SET IT UP CAREFULLY
choices.outcome: Managed well, it is free reach that actually converts.

choices.label: KEEP THE BUILD LOCKED DOWN
choices.outcome: No leak risk, no coverage either.

title: BENEFITS
body: The team has asked, politely and repeatedly, about a proper pension contribution.

choices.label: SET ONE UP
choices.outcome: An ongoing cost, and a real signal that this is a place to stay.

choices.label: PROMISE TO REVISIT IT
choices.outcome: The same conversation will happen again next year.

title: PROCESS
body: {name} wants to make code review mandatory, and some of the team are pushing back.

choices.label: BACK THE POLICY
choices.outcome: Slower merges, fewer fires. The pushback fades within a month.

choices.label: KEEP IT OPTIONAL
choices.outcome: Reviews happen when people remember. Bugs happen when they do not.

title: AN ART BOOK
body: A publisher wants to put out a small art book of one of your games.

choices.label: APPROVE IT
choices.outcome: A lovely object, a trickle of revenue, and the art team floating for weeks.

choices.label: PASS
choices.outcome: The idea goes nowhere.

title: CONTRACT CLIENT
body: A contract client keeps changing the brief without changing the deadline.

choices.label: HOLD THE LINE IN WRITING
choices.outcome: A firm, professional email resets expectations. Mostly.

choices.label: KEEP ABSORBING IT
choices.outcome: The team eats the churn. Morale and the schedule both slip.

title: A BREAKTHROUGH
body: {name}, still fairly new, has solved something the seniors had been stuck on.

choices.label: MAKE A POINT OF IT
choices.outcome: Public credit for a junior does more for the floor than a bonus would.

choices.label: A QUIET WELL DONE
choices.outcome: {name} appreciates it, even if nobody else hears.

title: END OF YEAR
body: It is the end of the year and the team is looking at you about a party.

choices.label: DO IT PROPERLY
choices.outcome: A good night out. People talk about it into January.

choices.label: DRINKS AT THE OFFICE
choices.outcome: Cheaper, flatter, fine.

title: FOCUS TIME
body: {name} says the open floor makes deep work almost impossible some afternoons.

choices.label: CREATE A QUIET ROOM
choices.outcome: A corner becomes a no-meeting, no-talking room. It fills up fast.

choices.label: SUGGEST HEADPHONES
choices.outcome: {name} has tried headphones. That was the point.

title: LEGACY SUPPORT
body: Players of a game you shipped years ago are asking for a compatibility patch.

choices.label: PATCH IT
choices.outcome: A week of someone's time buys years more goodwill from a loyal group.

choices.label: MARK IT UNSUPPORTED
choices.outcome: An honest notice. Some fans take it hard.

title: THE ENERGY BILL
body: The quarterly energy bill is far higher than budgeted.

choices.label: AUDIT AND FIX
choices.outcome: An efficiency sweep pays for itself by the next quarter.

choices.label: JUST PAY IT
choices.outcome: The hit lands in full this month.

title: A CHANGE OF SCENE
body: {name} has quietly asked to move to the other team for a while.

choices.label: ARRANGE THE SWAP
choices.outcome: A fresh problem re-energises {name}, and cross-pollinates both teams.

choices.label: KEEP THE TEAMS STABLE
choices.outcome: {name} stays put, and stays a little restless.

title: A CRITICAL ARTICLE
body: An outlet has run a pointed piece questioning one of the studio's design choices.

choices.label: RESPOND ONCE, CALMLY
choices.outcome: A measured reply and then silence. It reads as confidence.

choices.label: DO NOT ENGAGE
choices.outcome: The piece circulates unanswered for a week.

title: A STAKE IN IT
body: {name} has asked, seriously, about some form of ownership or profit share.

choices.label: START THAT CONVERSATION
choices.outcome: No promises today, but the fact you engaged means a lot.

choices.label: DEFLECT
choices.outcome: {name} reads the deflection accurately.

title: BUILD TIMES
body: Builds have crept up to twenty minutes and the whole team feels it.

choices.label: BUY A PROPER BUILD MACHINE
choices.outcome: Builds drop to three minutes. The floor audibly exhales.

choices.label: LIVE WITH IT
choices.outcome: Twenty minutes, forty times a day, across the team.

title: RETURN TO WORK
body: An experienced developer coming back from a long career break has applied for a trial.

choices.label: GIVE THEM THE TRIAL
choices.outcome: A bit of ramp-up, then a strong, grateful hire the market overlooked.

choices.label: GO WITH A SAFER CV
choices.outcome: You hire the obvious candidate instead.

title: A LETTER FROM A PLAYER
body: A player with limited vision has written about how close one of your games came to being playable for them.

choices.label: BUDGET AN ACCESSIBILITY PASS
choices.outcome: A few weeks of work opens the game to a lot more people.

choices.label: REPLY WITH THANKS
choices.outcome: A kind reply, and the game stays as it is.

title: THE HOURS
body: Nobody called a crunch, but people have been staying late for a month.

choices.label: CALL IT OUT AND SEND PEOPLE HOME
choices.outcome: You name the drift and stop it. The team believes you meant it.

choices.label: LET IT RIDE TO THE MILESTONE
choices.outcome: The milestone lands. So does the resentment.

title: A RIVAL FOLDS
body: A studio down the road has shut down, and some good people are suddenly available.

choices.label: REACH OUT WARMLY
choices.outcome: You are not hiring today, but you make the calls anyway. It is remembered.

choices.label: NOTE IT AND MOVE ON
choices.outcome: The moment passes.

title: AN HONEST ADMISSION
body: {name} owns up that an estimate {they} gave was badly wrong, early enough to matter.

choices.label: THANK THEM FOR THE HONESTY
choices.outcome: You replan calmly. The lesson is that honesty here is safe.

choices.label: MAKE AN EXAMPLE OF IT
choices.outcome: The schedule is fixed; the next bad estimate will be hidden.

title: THE FORUMS
body: The community around your games has outgrown anyone's spare time to manage it.

choices.label: GIVE SOMEONE THE ROLE OFFICIALLY
choices.outcome: Part of one person's week, formally. The forums calm down.

choices.label: KEEP MUDDLING THROUGH
choices.outcome: Threads go unanswered. The mood there slowly sours.

title: REARRANGING THE FLOOR
body: The team wants to reorganise the desks around how people actually work together.

choices.label: BLOCK OUT AN AFTERNOON
choices.outcome: A disruptive afternoon, then weeks of smoother collaboration.

choices.label: LEAVE IT AS IS
choices.outcome: The layout stays. So does the friction it causes.

title: A PROMISING PROTOTYPE
body: {name} has a rough prototype that everyone who plays it keeps thinking about.

choices.label: GIVE IT A REAL WEEK
choices.outcome: Nothing is promised, but the idea gets a fair shot.

choices.label: PARK IT FOR NOW
choices.outcome: The prototype goes in the drawer with the others.

title: A SLOW MONTH
body: Revenue this month is well down and the team can feel the mood shift.

choices.label: BE STRAIGHT WITH EVERYONE
choices.outcome: An honest all-hands about the numbers steadies people more than silence would.

choices.label: KEEP IT UPSTAIRS
choices.outcome: The uncertainty spreads in the gaps where information should be.

title: INSTITUTIONAL MEMORY
body: {name} has been here longer than anyone and holds a lot of undocumented knowledge.

choices.label: FUND A WEEK OF WRITING IT DOWN
choices.outcome: A dull week that de-risks the studio for years.

choices.label: TRUST IT STAYS IN THEIR HEAD
choices.outcome: It does, until the day it does not.

title: THE SNACK BUDGET
body: There is a surprisingly heated discussion about whether the studio should stock snacks.

choices.label: JUST STOCK THE KITCHEN
choices.outcome: A trivial cost that removes a recurring low-grade irritation.

choices.label: PEOPLE CAN BRING THEIR OWN
choices.outcome: Technically fair. Slightly mean.

title: AN EMBARGO BREAKS EARLY
body: A preview of your unannounced game has leaked a day before the planned reveal.

choices.label: BRING THE REVEAL FORWARD
choices.outcome: You get ahead of it within hours. The scramble is worth it.

choices.label: STICK TO THE PLAN
choices.outcome: The official reveal lands into a conversation that already happened.

title: AN OFFSITE
body: Someone has floated a two-day team offsite to plan the next year properly.

choices.label: BOOK IT
choices.outcome: Away from the desks, the team actually agrees on a direction.

choices.label: A LONG MEETING INSTEAD
choices.outcome: You cover the agenda in a room. Half of it does not stick.

title: LUNCH AND LEARN
body: A few people want to run weekly lunchtime sessions teaching each other their disciplines.

choices.label: SUPPORT IT
choices.outcome: The studio gets broader, more curious, and a little more bonded.

choices.label: KEEP LUNCH AS LUNCH
choices.outcome: The idea does not survive the first busy week.

title: A CONTRACTOR LEAVES
body: A contractor the team leaned on has finished up, and there is a hole where they were.

choices.label: BACKFILL PROPERLY
choices.outcome: A short, expensive scramble to bring someone else up to speed.

choices.label: SPREAD THE WORK
choices.outcome: The team covers it. Everyone is stretched a little thinner.

title: A DATA REQUEST
body: A researcher has asked, transparently, for anonymised play data from one of your games for a study.

choices.label: SHARE IT CAREFULLY
choices.outcome: A cautious yes, with the players' interests kept front of mind.

choices.label: DECLINE ON PRINCIPLE
choices.outcome: A clean no. The safest call, and a defensible one.

title: A FLAT PATCH
body: Nothing is wrong exactly, but the floor has felt low-energy for a couple of weeks.

choices.label: SHIP A SMALL WIN
choices.outcome: You carve out a tiny, finishable thing. Crossing it off lifts everyone.

choices.label: WAIT FOR IT TO PASS
choices.outcome: It does, eventually, on its own.

title: A REFERRAL
body: {name} knows someone excellent who might be tempted to join.

choices.label: PURSUE IT AND PAY THE BONUS
choices.outcome: A warm lead is worth ten cold CVs. {name} is pleased to have helped.

choices.label: ADD THEM TO THE PILE
choices.outcome: The contact goes into the applicant tracker with everyone else.

title: SECOND THOUGHTS
body: {name} thinks the engine decision made last year is quietly costing the team every week.

choices.label: SCHEDULE A REAL EVALUATION
choices.outcome: You commit to measuring it properly rather than arguing about it.

choices.label: IT IS TOO LATE TO CHANGE
choices.outcome: Probably true. It still lands badly.

title: A DEVELOPMENT GRANT
body: The studio qualifies for a modest regional development grant, with a form and a wait.

choices.label: DO THE PAPERWORK
choices.outcome: A tedious week for someone, then a genuinely useful cheque.

choices.label: NOT WORTH THE HASSLE
choices.outcome: The deadline passes.

title: A CAMEO
body: Another studio has asked to put a small nod to one of your characters in their game.

choices.label: SAY YES, WARMLY
choices.outcome: A friendly gesture that both fanbases enjoy spotting.

choices.label: KEEP THE IP CLEAN
choices.outcome: A polite no. Understandable, slightly joyless.

title: A ROUGH START
body: {name} joined a month ago and still does not have the access or docs to be productive.

choices.label: FIX ONBOARDING PROPERLY
choices.outcome: A day spent writing it down means the next hire does not lose a month.

choices.label: GET THEM UNBLOCKED FOR NOW
choices.outcome: {name} can work again. The next new starter hits the same wall.

title: TOO MANY MEETINGS
body: The calendar has filled with recurring meetings and the makers are visibly frustrated.

choices.label: CANCEL HALF OF THEM
choices.outcome: A brave cull. Two weeks later nobody misses the ones you dropped.

choices.label: KEEP THEM, TRIM THE AGENDAS
choices.outcome: A smaller fix. The calendar stays crowded.

title: A FAN CONVENTION
body: Fans are organising a small convention around games like yours and want the studio there.

choices.label: SHOW UP PROPERLY
choices.outcome: A weekend of your time, and a fanbase that now feels genuinely seen.

choices.label: SEND A CARE PACKAGE
choices.outcome: Some swag in the post. Appreciated, but not the same.

title: IN OVER THEIR HEAD
body: {name} was handed a task well beyond their level and is quietly drowning in it.

choices.label: RESCOPE AND PAIR THEM UP
choices.outcome: You catch it in time. {name} learns instead of breaking.

choices.label: LET THEM PUSH THROUGH
choices.outcome: {name} delivers something, late and shaky, and loses confidence.

title: SUSTAINABILITY
body: A few people want the studio to take its environmental footprint seriously.

choices.label: MAKE SOME REAL CHANGES
choices.outcome: Better suppliers, less waste, a small cost, and a team that is prouder of the place.

choices.label: PUT UP RECYCLING BINS
choices.outcome: A gesture. Better than nothing, and clearly just a gesture.

title: PRESERVATION
body: A games-preservation group has asked for source and assets from an old title, for the archive.

choices.label: CONTRIBUTE IT
choices.outcome: A little legal care, and a piece of the studio's work is safe for good.

choices.label: NOT RIGHT NOW
choices.outcome: Maybe when there is time. There is never time.

title: THE OTHER TEAM
body: {name} feels the two teams have drifted into an unhelpful us-and-them.

choices.label: MIX THEM DELIBERATELY
choices.outcome: A shared demo day and a couple of swaps thaw it out.

choices.label: LET EACH TEAM DO ITS THING
choices.outcome: The divide hardens a little more.

title: AN UNSOLICITED SHOUT-OUT
body: A well-known developer has praised one of your games, unprompted, in an interview.

choices.label: SHARE IT WITH THE TEAM
choices.outcome: A genuine lift, and a small bump in applications that week.

choices.label: STAY COOL ABOUT IT
choices.outcome: It still makes the group chat.

title: A CLIENT PAYS LATE
body: A contract client's payment is a month overdue and cash is tighter than it should be.

choices.label: CHASE IT FIRMLY
choices.outcome: An uncomfortable call, and the money lands within the week.

choices.label: WAIT POLITELY
choices.outcome: It arrives eventually. The gap it left did real damage to the month.

title: STUCK
body: {name} has plateaued and knows it, and it is starting to affect {their} mood.

choices.label: FUND A STRETCH PROJECT
choices.outcome: A harder problem, a bit of slack, and {name} climbs again.

choices.label: KEEP THEM ON STEADY WORK
choices.outcome: Reliable output, a slowly flattening person.
